facts.fact_text: The case concerns the applicant's criminal conviction for acts of mass disorder and violence against the police during the suppression of a demonstration at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow on 6 May 2012.
The background facts relating to the planning, conduct and dispersal of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square are set out in more detail in Frumkin v. Russia (no. 74568/12, §§ 7-65, 5 January 2016).

The background facts relating to the planning, conduct and dispersal of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square are set out in more detail in Yaroslav Belousov v. Russia (nos. 2653/13 and 60980/14, §§ 7-33, 4 October 2016).
At the time of the events of 6 May 2012, the applicant was a political activist.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he arrived at Kaluzhskaya Square in Moscow to take part in the 'March of Millions'.

According to the applicant, at around 6.50 p.m. on 6 May 2012 he found himself near Malyy Kamennyy Bridge in a crowd surrounded by police officers who were beating the protestors with truncheons and arresting them.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that on 6 May 2012 at 5 p.m. at the latest the applicant arrived at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow to take part in the demonstration.
The case concerns the applicant's criminal conviction for acts of mass disorder and violence against the police during the suppression of a demonstration at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow on 6 May 2012.
According to the applicant, four police officers eventually grabbed him and escorted him to a police car, which took him to a police station.
On 22 October 2014 the applicant was arrested.
On 26 February 2015 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow ordered the applicant's house arrest until 6 April 2015.

On 27 February 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence and destruction of property).
On 27 February 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).

On 3 April 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence and destruction of property).
On 3 April 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).
On 22 December 2015 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found the applicant guilty as charged.
The applicant was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment.
The applicant appealed against the judgment of the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow of 22 December 2015.
On 26 April 2016 the Moscow City Court upheld the first-instance judgment of the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow of 22 December 2015.

On 27 February 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence and destruction of property).
On 27 February 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).

On 3 April 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence and destruction of property).
On 3 April 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).
The relevant provisions of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation can be found in Frumkin v. Russia, no. 74568/12, § 78, 5 January 2016.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that between 5 p.m. and 10 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the applicant took part in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence against police officers and the destruction of property.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant defied lawful orders of the police and military and tried to break through the police cordon on 6 May 2012.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that unidentified participants of acts of mass disorder threw chunks of tarmac, stones, sticks and other objects at the police, which hit them.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant used violence against Police Officers K. and G. which did not endanger their life or health.
The background facts relating to the planning, conduct and dispersal of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square are set out in more detail in Frumkin v. Russia (no. 74568/12, §§ 7-65, 5 January 2016).

The background facts relating to the planning, conduct and dispersal of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square are set out in more detail in Yaroslav Belousov v. Russia (nos. 2653/13 and 60980/14, §§ 7-33, 4 October 2016).

According to the applicant, at around 6.50 p.m. on 6 May 2012 he found himself near Malyy Kamennyy Bridge in a crowd surrounded by police officers who were beating the protestors with truncheons and arresting them.
According to the applicant, a police officer attacked him using a truncheon on 6 May 2012.
According to the applicant, he was outraged and scared as a result of the police officer's attack.
According to the applicant, he tried to protect himself from the blows by extending his arms forward and distancing himself from the police.
Police Officer G. testified on 25 August 2015 that the applicant's actions caused Police Officer G. pain but that he sustained no injuries.
Ms N. testified on 1 December 2015 that during the clashes between protestors and the police at Bolotnaya Square she had been knocked down at some point.
Ms N. testified on 1 December 2015 that the applicant and other persons had helped her to stand up after she had been knocked down.
Ms N. testified on 1 December 2015 that after helping her stand up, the applicant had joined a group of people within six metres from her.
Ms N. testified on 1 December 2015 that at some point the applicant had been pulled out of the crowd and arrested by the police.
Ms N. testified on 1 December 2015 that the applicant had neither acted aggressively nor resisted his arrest.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant, acting with the intention of using violence, tried to prevent police officers from arresting aggressive participants of the demonstration.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant, standing in front of Police Officers K. and G., hit Police Officer K. in his left hand at least once.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant hit Police Officer G. in his left hand at least once.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant hit Police Officer K. in the head with his umbrella.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant hit Police Officer G. at least once in the left hand, causing both Police Officers K. and G. pain.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow described the video recording as showing police officers beginning to arrest the young man, who resisted arrest, hit one police officer in the helmet with his umbrella and in the hands, and hit another police officer at least twice in the hands.
The applicant was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment.

The applicant's sentence of two years and six months' imprisonment was calculated on the basis of a two-year prison term under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, partly concurrent with a term of one year and six months under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

In his appeal, the applicant argued that the statements of Police Officer G. given in 2012, soon after the events at Bolotnaya Square, confirmed that Police Officer G. had sustained neither injuries nor pain.
The applicant was released on 24 August 2017, having served his prison term.
